questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation keeps riders close together while maintaining safe distance?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while maintaining safe distance. Use single-file when riding through curves, turning, or entering/leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: Protect your eyes and your face.
Protect your face but not your eyes.
Protect your eyes, but not your face.
Not protect your face or eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield is needed to protect your entire face in a crash.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this makes wobbling worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road when safe. Avoid braking, as it can make wobbling worse.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wearing bright colors and reflective materials at all times makes you more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, where should you look?

options.text: Keep your eyes focused close to the front of the motorcycle.
Look through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Increase your speed before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, how should you brake?

options.text: Apply the brakes more firmly than usual to stop quickly.
Apply the brakes more softly than usual to keep from overworking them.

questions.explanation: A passenger in a sidecar adds weight and affects how your motorcycle handles. You will need more distance to stop. Start slowing down sooner than you normally would.

questions.question: How should a group of riders pass another vehicle?
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider waits until the first rider has safely returned to the original lane before passing. Continue this pattern until all riders have passed.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. Speed limit signs are regulatory signs. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way for a rider to be more visible?

options.text: Using your headlight at all times

questions.explanation: To be visible, wear bright clothing with reflective materials. Use your headlight at all times. Use your signals and brake light correctly. Waving does not help other drivers see you.

questions.question: If road conditions need a longer stopping distance, you should:

options.text: Ask someone else to ride your motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if your motorcycle needs more time to stop. Do this on slippery pavement, if you cannot see ahead, or if traffic is heavy. Use at least a three-second following distance.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Avoid using your high beam headlight.

questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances in the dark. Reduce your speed and increase your following distance when riding at night. Use your high beam when you are not meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: Increase your following distance:

options.text: If there are only a few vehicles on the roadway.
If drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more time to stop. Do this on slippery pavement, if you cannot see the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy and another driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ______ or higher is legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to ride a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean when the operator leans. Sit as far forward as you can without crowding the operator. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If you can do so safely, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may only make them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes involve:

options.text: Riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when riding a motorcycle that is new to you. Most motorcycle crashes involve operators who have less than six months of experience on that specific bike.

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: When shifting to a lower gear, shift down one gear at a time. Ease out the clutch through the friction zone between each downshift.

questions.question: Riders not wearing helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders wearing helmets.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets, regardless of speed.

questions.question: What is the best protection for a motorcycle operator?

options.text: Keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid hitting other vehicles is to keep distance between you and them. Extra space gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes. Wearing proper gear is also important.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic face shield that resists impact gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Regular eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough. In Vermont, you do not need eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still a good idea.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least three-quarters of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What helmet gives you the most protection?

options.text: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
A helmet that has been in a crash before.
A helmet that protects your hearing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards for the best protection. Your helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: When riding at night, which action should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.explanation: To be safe when riding at night, slow down and stay farther away from other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead of you to see the road better. Use your high beam headlight, except when you are following or meeting another vehicle.
